comments.text: I'm a GenX engineer in Si Valley that has always enjoyed wrenching on cars/motorcycles for fun as a hobby. We have a new one for the woman (2026 RAV4 plug in Hybrid and pretty happy with it, even with the extra tech) and I keep the older vehicles for my entertainment 2001 Audi, 1997 GMC Yukon, and 2005 Nissan XTerra that are all fairly dependable, well designed and built and has been easy to find parts for thus far. Many of our friends have EVs but we are not ready for that jump yet due to many issues with the tech, resale, and charging infrastructure. I agree with the man on not doing what you enjoy as a hobby for a job because you will learn to hate it. I think we have a shortage of fair pay and it will bounce back when there are no more technicians in due time (Unionize!!!). But newer cars, EV or otherwise, are not desirable, dependable, or fun to wrench on. Just expensive throw away consumables like smart phones. We need to step back and really look at what we are doing. Too many bells and whistles that can break, no reliability being engineered to break, right to repair laws, and poor resale of EVs is not sustainable.
